newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's CentralPower posts NZ$2.42 mln half yr profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's CentralPower posts NZ$2.42 mln half yr profit.

text.p: Unlisted Manawatu power company CentralPower Ltd late on Monday reported a net profit of NZ$2.42 million for the six months to September 30, 1996.

This compared with an $11.15 million first-half profit last year, which was boosted by gains on the sale and market revaluation of shares in Wairarapa Electricity and Energy Direct (now part of TransAlta NZ, 63 percent owned by Canada's TransAlta Corp ).
CentralPower said this year's six-month profit was a 17 percent improvement over the same period last year on a comparative basis and eight percent ahead of budget.
CentralPower said trading sales decreased 5.8 percent to $22.56 million while depreciation costs increased by $1.24 million resulting from the revaluation of the company's network assets.

"The decrease in trading sales reflects the loss of a small number of larger energy customers. While this had an effect on revenue, the effect on profit is very small given the low margin on these sales and the retention of the network services," CentralPower said.
Associate company Energy Brokers New Zealand Ltd secured a number of the energy contracts previously held by CentralPower and made a $330,000 contribution to the half year profit result.
CentralPower said it would pay a fully imputed dividend of three cents per share on November 29.
